title: Legal Assessment
subtitle: Professional expert opinions, defence memoranda, and positions of human rights bodies.
intro: This section consolidates the intellectual basis of the defence. It brings together documents demonstrating the groundlessness of the prosecution from the standpoint of international law, fundamental human rights, and arbitration rulings that have entered into force.

sections.title: Serbian Defence (Extradition Proceedings)
sections.content: Procedural documents and memoranda submitted to Belgrade courts.
sections.summary: Legal establishment of the commercial nature of the conflict. The defence consistently demonstrates that the extradition request rests on a transaction whose lawfulness has been confirmed by arbitration rulings. This is a legal barrier against the attempt to criminalise civil relations.

sections.title: Human Rights Dimension
sections.content: Conclusions and positions of independent institutions on the risks of arbitrary prosecution.
sections.summary: The case is characterised as one violating fair trial standards. Human rights experts analyse the disproportionality of the criminal pressure and point to the use of law enforcement in the interests of parties to a corporate conflict.

sections.title: Professional Legal Expert Analysis
sections.content: Analytical notes, expert opinions, and memoranda by international law practitioners.
sections.summary: Detailed analysis of the legal contradictions in the case. Experts examine the absence of corpus delicti, the groundlessness of the 'conspiracy' charges, and the legal consequences of disregarding arbitration rulings in criminal proceedings.

sections.title: Inverted Interpretation: How the Investigation Reads Its Own Evidence
sections.content: Analysis of three key episodes from inspection records (December 2022, November 2023), where the investigation reaches conclusions directly opposite to what is recorded in those same documents.

episodes.label: 'The value must be real' = evidence of a conspiracy to understate value
episodes.what_protocol_says: CRM correspondence, 01.12.2021, 10:11: Lagovski D.V. writes to Osipova M.V. — 'the value must be real.' The inspection record (17.12.2022) reproduces this phrase verbatim and characterises it as evidence that the parties agreed on a below-market valuation.
episodes.what_it_actually_means: 'Real value' is market value. A person seeking an understated appraisal writes 'give us a lower number,' not 'the value must be real.' The phrase is the direct opposite of what the investigation infers from it. If there had been a conspiracy to understate — this very phrase would be the principal evidence against the investigation's own theory.

episodes.label: 'Illogical' trip to collect the report = evidence of criminal intent
episodes.what_protocol_says: The inspection record (17.12.2022) characterises Lagovski's visit to the offices of LLC 'Company for Valuation and Law' on 14.07.2021 to collect the original of report No. 2021/447 as 'illogical and not required by his duties' — and draws from this a conclusion about a link to criminal intent.
episodes.what_it_actually_means: From the same CRM correspondence recorded in the same protocol, it follows that the original of report No. 2021/447 had been sent to Lagovski by post back in April 2021. The July visit was a follow-up request for a physical copy, as directly reflected in the correspondence. The 'illogicality' of the trip is explained in the very materials the investigation cites as evidence.
episodes.source: Inspection record of 17.12.2022, pp. 9–10 (CRM correspondence, tab 'Client correspondence')

episodes.label: 'Ira thanks sent in pdf' = evidence of conspiracy with the appraiser
episodes.what_protocol_says: The inspection record (November 2023, telephone of Sorokina I.O.) reproduces WhatsApp correspondence between the management of LLC 'KOP'. Sorokina I.O.'s reply 'Ira thanks sent in pdf' is included in the body of facts that, according to the investigation, 'indicate that the employees of LLC KOP agreed to produce a report with an understated value.'
episodes.what_it_actually_means: 'Sent in pdf' is a standard office acknowledgement that a finished document has been dispatched. This is a phrase from any office correspondence of any appraisal company in any country. Neither in this message nor in the surrounding context is there a word about understating value, about an arrangement with the client, or about any departure from professional standards.
episodes.source: Inspection record of 03.11.2023 (iPhone 12 of Sorokina I.O.), WhatsApp correspondence

sections.summary: All three episodes share one feature: the investigation quotes documents accurately but interprets them in a direction directly opposite to their plain meaning. This is not a misreading — it is a systemic method. Readers can verify: the primary sources are open.

summary: This section presents the consolidated position of leading legal experts. It assembles the arguments demonstrating the need to return the case to the rule of law and to end the unlawful prosecution.

theses.title: Protection of the Legal Profession: UN Principles
theses.text: The prosecution of Dmitry Lagovsky is a direct attack on the independence of the legal profession. Under the UN Basic Principles on the Role of Lawyers, lawyers shall not be identified with their clients or their clients' causes as a result of discharging their professional functions. By seeking to extradite a lawyer for professional advice on compliance with market standards, Serbia sets a dangerous precedent: any lawyer anywhere in the world may now be arrested at a third country's request for doing their job in good faith. This is the complete destruction of the principle of Legal Certainty. If a professional opinion can constitute a criminal offence, law as an institution ceases to exist.
theses.source: UN Basic Principles on the Role of Lawyers (1990), Principle 18

theses.title: Corporate Dispute and Criminal Raiding
theses.text: This case is a textbook example of how a local corporate conflict — entirely lost by a minority shareholder in the highest arbitration courts — is artificially converted into a criminal matter. The criminal case is used here not to protect the law, but as an instrument of retaliation and leverage in a private commercial dispute. The lawyer was chosen as the most convenient target: a 'procedural hostage' whose prosecution is meant to paralyse the company's defence. The Serbian court's disregard for rulings by the Russian arbitration courts and the Supreme Court of the Russian Federation — all of which confirmed the lawfulness of the transaction — points to a critical failure in the judicial filter applied to extradition requests.
theses.source: Russian arbitration court rulings including the Supreme Court, 2024–2025

theses.title: The Absurdity of the Charges: Res Judicata and Actual Sentences
theses.text: The charges against Lagovsky rest on alleged 'undervaluation' in a transaction that the Supreme Court of the requesting state has officially recognised as market-priced and lawful. Moreover, the principal defendants in the case — the directors and owners of the companies — have already received suspended sentences of 1.8 years in Russia. In this context, the demand to extradite a legal consultant in order to place him in pre-trial detention constitutes a flagrant act of legal arbitrariness. Extradition arrest and deportation in a case that the requesting state itself considers not to warrant actual imprisonment for the organisers violates the principle of proportionality and Articles 5 and 6 of the ECHR.
